School.title: School
School.description: Represents a school, which acts as a distinct tenant within the multi-tenant system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the School entity (Tenant ID).

name.description: The official name of the school.

address.description: The physical address of the school.

contactEmail.description: The primary contact email address for the school.

contactPhone.description: The primary contact phone number for the school.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account within the school management system with defined roles and access permissions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

schoolId.description: Reference to the School the user is associated with. (Relationship: School 1:N User)

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

email.description: The primary email address of the user.

role.description: The assigned role of the user within the school (e.g., 'SchoolOwner', 'Headmaster', 'Teacher', 'Bursar', 'Parent', 'MaintenanceStaff').

Asset.title: Asset
Asset.description: Represents a physical asset or property owned by the school, such as furniture, IT equipment, or supplies, requiring inventory and maintenance tracking.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Asset entity.

schoolId.description: Reference to the School that owns this asset. (Relationship: School 1:N Asset)

qrCodeValue.description: A unique string value generated for this asset, intended to be encoded in a QR code for quick identification and lookup when scanned.

name.description: The common name or title of the asset (e.g., 'Classroom Projector', 'Student Chair', 'Office Printer').

assetTag.description: An optional alphanumeric tag or serial number physically affixed to the asset for additional identification.

description.description: A detailed description providing more context about the asset.

category.description: The classification category of the asset (e.g., 'IT Equipment', 'Classroom Furniture', 'Sports Equipment', 'Office Supplies').

location.description: The specific physical location within the school where the asset is primarily kept or used (e.g., 'Room 101', 'Admin Office', 'Science Lab').

purchaseDate.description: The date when the asset was acquired by the school.

purchasePrice.description: The monetary cost of the asset at the time of purchase.

warrantyEndDate.description: The date on which the manufacturer's or vendor's warranty for the asset expires.

status.description: The current operational condition or availability status of the asset (e.g., 'Operational', 'Under Maintenance', 'Faulty', 'Retired', 'Missing').

MaintenanceLog.title: MaintenanceLog
MaintenanceLog.description: Records individual maintenance, repair, or inspection events performed on a specific school asset.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MaintenanceLog entity.

assetId.description: Reference to the Asset that this maintenance log entry pertains to. (Relationship: Asset 1:N MaintenanceLog)

schoolId.description: Reference to the School that owns the asset being maintained. (Relationship: School 1:N MaintenanceLog)

maintenanceDate.description: The date and time when the maintenance activity was performed.

description.description: A detailed narrative describing the work done, issues found, or parts replaced during maintenance.

performedByUserId.description: Reference to the User (e.g., maintenance staff) who performed or oversaw the maintenance. (Relationship: User 1:N MaintenanceLog)

cost.description: The monetary cost incurred for this specific maintenance event (e.g., labor, parts).

statusAfterMaintenance.description: The operational status of the asset immediately following this maintenance event (e.g., 'Operational', 'Still Faulty', 'Repaired', 'Requires Further Action').

definition.description: Root collection for each school tenant. All data for a school is nested under its respective schoolId, ensuring strict multi-tenancy and data isolation.

params.name: schoolId
params.description: The unique identifier for the School.

definition.description: Stores user profiles and roles specific to a school. The user's schoolId is implicitly denormalized from the path, and their role is stored within the document for DBAC.

params.name: schoolId
params.description: The unique identifier of the School the user belongs to.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the User, typically matching Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Stores details of physical assets belonging to a school. Includes schoolId for multi-tenancy. The qrCodeValue field facilitates lookups within the school's context.

params.name: schoolId
params.description: The unique identifier of the School that owns this asset.

params.name: assetId
params.description: The unique identifier for the Asset.

definition.description: Records individual maintenance, repair, or inspection events performed on a specific school asset. Includes denormalized schoolId, assetId for path-based access, and denormalized 'performedByUserRole' and 'performedByUserSchoolId' for authorization independence.

params.name: schoolId
params.description: The unique identifier of the School that owns the asset being maintained.

params.name: assetId
params.description: The unique identifier for the Asset to which this log entry pertains.

params.name: maintenanceLogId
params.description: The unique identifier for the MaintenanceLog entry.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for ShuleDirect Pro adopts a multi-tenant, hierarchical design, anchoring all school-specific data under a dedicated root collection for each school. This strategy is critical for ensuring data isolation, simplifying access control, and optimizing query performance in a multi-school environment. The core principle of Authorization Independence is achieved through strategic denormalization and path-based ownership.

1.  **Multi-Tenancy and Structural Segregation:** The top-level `/schools/{schoolId}` collection serves as the tenant boundary. All subsequent collections, such as `users`, `assets`, and `maintenanceLogs`, are subcollections nested under a specific `schoolId`. This inherently segregates data by school, fulfilling the 'Structural Segregation' mandate by ensuring that documents within each subcollection pertain to a single tenant and share a homogeneous security posture. This dramatically simplifies security rules, as all rules can implicitly assume the `schoolId` from the path.

2.  **Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
    *   For `User` and `Asset` entities, the `schoolId` is included in their respective paths (`/schools/{schoolId}/users/{userId}` and `/schools/{schoolId}/assets/{assetId}`). This means that when checking access to a user or an asset, the `schoolId` can be directly accessed from the request path, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to a parent `School` document to establish the tenant context. This prevents hierarchical authorization dependencies.
    *   For `MaintenanceLog` entries (`/schools/{schoolId}/assets/{assetId}/maintenanceLogs/{maintenanceLogId}`), the `schoolId` and `assetId` are available in the path. Crucially, to avoid a `get()` call to the `User` document to verify the `performedByUserId`'s role during a `create` or `update` operation, the `MaintenanceLog` document itself will include **denormalized fields `performedByUserRole` and `performedByUserSchoolId`**. The client application is responsible for writing these fields accurately based on the authenticated user's profile. Security rules will then validate that `request.auth.uid == request.resource.data.performedByUserId`, `request.resource.data.performedByUserRole == 'MaintenanceStaff'`, and `request.resource.data.performedByUserSchoolId == schoolId`, all without needing to perform a `get()` operation to verify the user's role in a separate document. This makes the `MaintenanceLog` document's authorization self-contained for the specific action.

3.  **QAPs (Query/Access Pattern Support):**
    *   **Secure `list` Operations:** By nesting data under `/schools/{schoolId}`, all queries for users, assets, or maintenance logs will be inherently scoped to a specific school. For instance, a query like `db.collection('schools').doc(schoolId).collection('assets')` will efficiently retrieve assets for only that school. This adheres to QAPs because security rules can enforce that `request.path.segments[1]` (the `schoolId` from the path) matches the authenticated user's `schoolId` (from their user profile) and role, thus preventing unauthorized data leakage through broad `list` queries.
    *   **QR Code Scanning:** The `Asset` entity includes `qrCodeValue`. When a QR code is scanned, assuming the user is already authenticated within a `schoolId` context, an efficient query like `db.collection('schools').doc(schoolId).collection('assets').where('qrCodeValue', '==', scannedValue)` can quickly retrieve the asset details. This avoids the need for a global collection group query or an additional mapping collection, keeping the structure aligned with the provided entities.

4.  **DBAC (Database Access Control):** User roles (`SchoolOwner`, `Headmaster`, `MaintenanceStaff`, etc.) are stored directly within each user's document at `/schools/{schoolId}/users/{userId}`. Security rules will use `request.auth.uid` to identify the current user and perform a `get()` call to *their own* user document to retrieve their `role` for granular permission checks (e.g., `allow read: if get(/databases/$(database)/documents/schools/$(schoolId)/users/$(request.auth.uid)).data.role == 'SchoolOwner'`). This is an accepted pattern for DBAC, as it checks the actor's authorization context rather than a hierarchical dependency on a separate data entity.

In summary, this structure provides a robust, scalable, and secure foundation by prioritizing multi-tenancy, strict authorization independence where critical, and efficient query patterns, all while aligning with the core design principles.
